Calculate the discriminant to check for real roots. If positive, two real solutions; if zero, one; if negative, complex. Plug in values and simplify step by step.

Differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug them back into f(x) to find y-values. Then, use the second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, it’s a local minimum; if < 0, a local maximum; if zero, inconclusive.
